thread:
maria.h: Heads-up — noticed a weird skew when running fractional cohort TTL + traffic-fuse during a small canary. cohorts with ~0.2% weight ended up getting almost exclusively routed to fallback (lots of fallback requests). :confused:
jonathan.k: Wait, "fractional cohort TTL" meaning the sampler sets a short TTL for cohort membership and the gateway has traffic_fuse that collapses low-qps routes? can you paste config?
tina.z: Yup. here's a redacted snippet from the canary we ran: 
```json
{
  "routes": [
    {"id": "exp-blue", "weight": 0.002, "match": {"header": "X-Experiment", "equals": "blue"}, "ttl_ms": 300000},
    {"id": "fallback", "weight": 0.998}
  ],
  "traffic_fuse": {"enabled": true, "threshold_qps": 100}
}
```
maria.h: Exactly. On paper weight=0.002 should get steady ~2qps for our traffic profile, but fuse seemed to flip to fallback during short spikes and never recovered for many sessions.
kevin.p: Hmm. traffic_fuse is global right now (it watches total routed qps per route group) not per-route. If the overall front-end qps dropped below threshold it collapses to fallback to avoid cold-starts. That would bias tiny cohorts.
jonathan.k: That seems dangerous for A/B fairness. Small cohorts will be systematically suppressed if fuse is aggressive. We need a math check: effective expected qps = total_qps * weight * (1/ttl_frequency?) not sure.
tina.z: In our case total_qps was ~1000, so expected for weight=0.002 => ~2 qps, but because of sampling TTL expiration and prefix-cache churn we saw bursts then long silences so the fuse saw <100 qps for that route group and collapsed it.
kevin.p: Suggestion: change fuse logic to consider per-route estimated qps (total_qps * route_weight) and only fuse if that estimate < configured threshold AND observed actual qps is < threshold for a sustained window. Basically avoid collapsing routes that are expected to be low but healthy.
maria.h: Could also add an explicit 'never_fuse' flag for experiment routes or a min_route_qps override in rollout config.
jonathan.k: We should also surface this in the console: a small-cohort warning when you create route weight < 0.5% with fuse enabled. The UX should recommend disabling fuse or setting min_route_qps.
tina.z: Agreed. I'll open a short RFC/PR to: 1) compute per-route expected_qps in router, 2) add an opt-in min_route_qps and never_fuse tag, 3) emit a telemetry metric `route.fuse_evaluations` with reason codes.
kevin.p: I'll add a Grafana panel for `route.fuse_evaluations` + per-route actual_qps vs expected_qps so we can catch regressions.
maria.h: Nice. Also let's add a regression test in traffic-sim that runs low-weight cohorts under fuse and asserts no >50% fallback skew unless overall infra under strain.
jonathan.k: One more edge: session-stickiness with headers can amplify the bias if sampler TTL is short. Maybe we should recommend longer TTLs for cohorts <1% to reduce prefix churn.
tina.z: noted. I'll include TTL guidance in the PR.
infra-bot: Deploy pipeline started for branch `router/fuse-per-route-estimate` (build #5821).
maria.h: :thumbsup: thanks. who wants to be reviewer for the router change?
kevin.p: happy to review the telemetry/dashboard bits.
jonathan.k: I'll review routing logic and tests.
tina.z: thanks — I'll aim to have the PR up today and ping both of you.
maria.h: Awesome. — follow-up: file a short postmortem if we see customer-facing noise, but likely internal canary only.
jonathan.k: ack.
kevin.p: ack.
